reply_text:
I found the quoted words on the page exactly as given, but the claim fails part 1. In August 2015 LeCun ran Facebook's research lab and was not yet its named chief scientist.

**1. The page.** It opened. It is Tom Simonite's MIT Technology Review feature "Teaching Machines to Understand Us", dated August 6, 2015. The quote matches word for word: "There is the same phenomenon that we were observing just before 2012," … "Things are starting to work, but the people doing more classical techniques are not convinced. Within a year or two it will be the end." This is a magazine feature that quotes him, not his own post, a transcript or a printed question-and-answer. So even if it got through, it could only be "pass, coverage only". The page gives the article's publication date (August 6, 2015), not the date of the interview itself.

**2. The rule.**
- **Part 1 (role) fails.** The article says Facebook "hired LeCun from NYU in December 2013 and put him in charge of a new artificial-intelligence research group, FAIR." His role history matches: founding director of FAIR from about 2013 to 2018, and Chief AI Scientist only from about 2018. The rule's chief scientist route needs "that company's named chief scientist speaking for it". In 2015 he did not hold that title. Running a lab inside Facebook is not being the company's chief executive, founder-leader or chair. The reviewer may want to confirm that a lab's founding director doesn't count, but the rule as written doesn't include it.
- **Part 2 (looks forward, about AI) is borderline.** Taken alone, "it will be the end" is mainly about doubters losing an argument. The paragraph around it ties it to deep learning mastering language, which does make it a forecast about AI. Still, the test would be loose: it is hard to say when doubters have been convinced.
- **Part 3 (date) passes.** "Within a year or two" is a stated span. Taking the later end gives a due date around August 2017.
- **Part 4 (source) only gets as far as coverage only.** The quote appears in news coverage, not in his own words, a transcript or a printed Q&A.
- **Recorded?** No. None of the listed claim files comes before 2023.

The same paragraph has another forecast: virtual helpers with unprecedented language skill "in just two to five years". The article gives it in its own words, not as a quote from him, and it fails part 1 for the same reason.
